@Edison Xie and I have implemented the following design in draft PR #43000, refactoring the definition of MonoidWithZeroHom.ValueGroup₀.

Currently, the definition of ValueGroup₀ f (the group range of a monoid-with-zero hom f : A₀ →*₀ B₀) is built in three steps:

  1. Take the smallest monoid containing the set-theoretic range of f, restricted to B₀ˣ (valueMonoid).
  2. Take the minimal group containing that monoid (valueGroup).
  3. Append a zero element to obtain ValueGroup₀ f := WithZero (valueGroup f).

This construction makes the canonical map from ValueGroup₀ f to B₀ awkward to define and leads to lengthy proofs, especially since one frequently has to discuss by cases whether an element is zero.

We propose the following alternative (see this file in the PR):
Develop SubgroupWithZero analogously to Subgroup, and then define valueGroup₀ f simply as SubgroupWithZero.closure (Set.range f).

This simplifies many downstream definitions—for example, ValueGroup₀.embedding becomes a subtype coercion, and ValueGroup₀.restrict becomes much cleaner. See changes in Mathlib/RingTheory/Valuation/Basic.lean.
It also allows us to clean up several proofs; for instance, embedding_strictMono is replaced by the more general lemma subtype_strictMono.

We further build on this idea of developing APIs directly for GroupWithZero, rather than translating everything to Group, to avoid translating between A₀ and WithZero A₀ˣ. In particular, we’ve introduced IsCyclicWithZero A₀ (meaning A₀ˣ is cyclic) and related results (such as zpower₀ and zpowersHom₀), which avoid many unnecessary coercions.

Any comments or suggestions would be appreciated. Thanks!
cc @Filippo A. E. Nuccio @María Inés de Frutos Fernández @Riccardo Brasca
I think splitting it up to make the subobjects first would make things cleaner.

Sure! May I know more about the motivation behind this? Is it mainly about the performance issue?
Performance and user-friendliness wrt dot notation and namespacing

One of the reason that initially brought us to define it the way we did was to have an efficient way of comparing the result of the following two constructions out of a monoid hom A ->* M:

  1. Extend it to A ->* M' where A' and M' are the groups generated by A and M, then add a zero element, and try to identify the initial image of A inside M'_0`
  2. First add zeroes to A and M, then create the relevant group with zero.

How would you do this in your setting?

Can you please give some more details about the specific scenario that we need this?
I made specific APIs for the case A=ZA = \mathbb{Z}A=Z (multiplicative). I think this may be the most common case that we need to define a map between monoid with zero hom starting from a monoid hom.

I don't think this PR is mainly about saving number of lines of codes. I hope this PR would make proofs closer to mathematical intuitions (value group is supposed to be the "image of a valuation", thus a subobject.) and easier to write (less by_cases). Developing whole theory of SubmonoidWithZero would certainly increase the totally number of lines of code.
Note that the development of SubmonoidWithZero and SubgroupWithZero could be separated out from this PR. This part can be merged into Mathlib even if we don't adopt the refactor of ValueGroup₀.
